chunks: And by this chain, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdِ Allāh عليه السلام saying: ‘Indeed, for al-Qāʾim there shall be a ghaybah before he rises. Indeed, he fears,’ and he gestured with his hand toward his belly, meaning killing.

key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: the one who will rise; a title of the Imam al-Mahdī عليه السلام
key_terms.الْقَتْلَ: killing; the intended meaning of the gesture mentioned in the hadith
key_terms.غَيْبَةً: occultation; a period of concealment from public appearance
key_terms.يَخَافُ: he fears; indicating danger before the rise
key_terms.يَقُومَ: to rise; to commence his mission openly

ai.seo_question: Why will al-Qāʾim عليه السلام have a ghaybah before his rise?
ai.summary: This hadith states that al-Qāʾim عليه السلام will have a ghaybah before his rise. It indicates that this occultation is connected to fear of being killed, and thus relates to the conditions preceding his divinely ordained appearance.

en.hubeali: And by this chain, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from his father Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘For Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup>, there would be an Occultation before he<sup>asws</sup> arises. He<sup>asws</sup> would fear’, and he<sup>asws</sup> gestured by his<sup>asws</sup> hand towards his<sup>asws</sup> belly, meaning the murder’.
en.sarwar: 18. Through the same chain of narrators it is narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father, Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Bukayr from Zurara who has said the following.

“ Al-Qa’im (the one who will rise with Divine Authority) will disappear before he will rise with divine power. He will suffer fear. The Imam (a.s.) pointed to his midsection, meaning thereby being murdered.”
